chapters.n: Simon Peter writes again, this time to all who share the same precious faith the Apostles have—a faith given through the righteousness of Jesus Christ, whom he calls both God and Savior.

f.g: Faith of equal value and honor.

chapters.n: Peter wishes them abundant grace and peace, which grow as we come to know God and Jesus.
God’s power has already given us everything we need for a godly life, through knowing Him who called us by His own glory and goodness.

f.g: Reverent devotion to God shown in daily life.

chapters.n: Through His great promises we can share in God’s own nature and escape the world’s corruption. Latter-day Saints see here the eternal potential of God’s children.
Peter lists a ladder of Christlike qualities, beginning with faith. Make every effort to add goodness to faith, and knowledge to goodness.
Add self-control to knowledge, endurance to self-control, and devotion to God to endurance.
Finally, add kindness toward fellow believers, and crown it all with charity, the pure love of Christ.
If these qualities are growing in you, your knowledge of Christ won’t be useless or fruitless.
Anyone lacking them is spiritually nearsighted—even blind—and has forgotten that his past sins were washed away.

f.g: Nearsighted; only able to see what is close.

chapters.n: So work all the harder to make your calling and election sure. Living this way keeps you from falling. Latter-day Saints connect this phrase with the more sure word of prophecy.
Then you will receive a rich welcome into the eternal kingdom of our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ.
Peter promises to keep reminding them, even though they already know and are grounded in the truth.
As long as he lives in this body, he thinks it right to stir them up with reminders.
Peter knows his death is near, just as Jesus told him. Tradition says he was martyred in Rome.
He wants to make sure they can recall these teachings after he is gone—perhaps one reason this letter was written.
The Apostles did not invent clever myths. They personally saw Christ’s majesty.
At the Transfiguration, God the Father gave Jesus honor and glory, declaring from heaven: “This is my beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased.”

f.g: The majestic glory—a reverent way of referring to God.

chapters.n: Peter, James, and John heard that voice themselves on the holy mountain.
The prophetic word is even more certain. Hold onto it like a lamp in a dark place until the day dawns and the morning star rises in your hearts.

f.g: The morning star, a symbol of Christ.

chapters.n: Most important: no prophecy in scripture comes from a prophet’s own private ideas or explanation.

f.g: Originating from a person’s own understanding. The JST wording stresses that prophecy is given by God, not man.

chapters.n: Prophecy never came from human will. Holy men spoke from God as the Holy Ghost carried them along.

f.g: Carried along, like a ship by the wind.

chapters.n: Just as false prophets appeared in ancient Israel, false teachers will arise in the Church, quietly introducing destructive ideas and even denying the Lord who bought them.
Many will follow their immoral ways, and because of them the true faith will be mocked.
Driven by greed, they will exploit believers with made-up stories. But their judgment is not idle—it is on its way.
Peter gives three examples of God’s judgment. First, God did not spare the angels who rebelled but cast them into darkness awaiting judgment.

f.g: Greek Tartarus — a place of confinement for rebels.

chapters.n: Second, God sent the Flood on the ungodly ancient world, yet preserved Noah, a preacher of righteousness, with seven others.

f.g: Noah plus seven others—eight in all.

chapters.n: Third, God reduced Sodom and Gomorrah to ashes as a warning to the ungodly who would come later.
Yet God rescued righteous Lot, who was distressed by the depraved conduct around him.
Living among them, Lot was tormented day after day by what he saw and heard.
The lesson: the Lord knows how to rescue the faithful from trials and to hold the wicked for judgment.
This applies especially to those who indulge corrupt desires and despise authority. They are arrogant and willful, unafraid to slander glorious beings.

f.g: Glorious ones—possibly angels or heavenly powers.

chapters.n: Even angels, though more powerful, don’t bring slanderous accusations against such beings before the Lord.
These teachers are like animals driven by instinct, mocking what they don’t understand, and they will be destroyed in their own corruption.
They will be paid back with harm for the harm they cause. They party openly even in daylight and are stains on the believers’ shared meals.
Their eyes are always looking for adultery and never tire of sin. They lure unstable people and have trained their hearts in greed—they are under a curse.
They have left the right path to follow Balaam, the prophet who loved the money he could earn by doing wrong.

f.g: Greek form of Beor, Balaam’s father.

chapters.n: Balaam was rebuked by his own donkey, which spoke with a human voice and stopped the prophet’s madness.

f.g: dumb = unable to speak; ass = donkey.

chapters.n: These teachers promise much but deliver nothing—like dry wells or clouds blown away before they rain. Deep darkness awaits them.
With boastful, empty words they use sensual desires to lure people who are just escaping from a life of error.
They promise freedom while being slaves to corruption themselves. Whatever overpowers a person becomes his master.
Those who escape the world’s filth by knowing Christ but then get tangled in it again end up worse off than before.
It would have been better never to have known the way of righteousness than to know it and turn away from God’s holy commandment.

f.w: better for them not to have known

chapters.n: Peter uses two blunt proverbs: a dog returns to its vomit, and a washed pig goes back to wallowing in the mud.

f.w: dog is turned to his own vomit

chapters.n: Peter mentions this is his second letter to them. In both he aims to stir up their sincere minds by reminding them of truths they already know.
He wants them to remember the words of the holy prophets and the commandments of the Lord given through His Apostles.
First, understand that in the last days mockers will come, living by their own desires.
They will sneer, “Where is His promised coming? Since our ancestors died, everything has stayed the same since creation.”

f.w: Where is the promise of his coming

chapters.n: They deliberately ignore that God’s word created the heavens and formed the earth out of and by water.
By that same water the earlier world was flooded and destroyed. Things have not always stayed the same.
The present heavens and earth are being kept by that same word for fire on the day of judgment. Latter-day Saints understand the earth will be cleansed by fire at Christ’s coming.
Don’t forget: to the Lord one day is like a thousand years and a thousand years like a day. God’s timing isn’t ours.

f.w: one day is with the Lord as a thousand years

chapters.n: The Lord isn’t slow to keep His promise. He is patient, wanting no one to perish but everyone to repent.

f.w: not willing that any should perish

chapters.n: Still, the day of the Lord will come unexpectedly like a thief. The heavens will pass away with a roar, and the elements will melt in intense heat.

f.w: as a thief in the night

chapters.n: Since everything around us will be dissolved, what kind of people should we be? Holy and godly in all we do.
Look forward to the day of God and even help hasten it, the day when the heavens burn and the elements melt.
But according to His promise, we look forward to new heavens and a new earth where righteousness lives. Latter-day Saints believe the earth will be renewed and receive paradisiacal glory.

f.w: new heavens and a new earth

chapters.n: So while you wait, work hard to be found by Him at peace, spotless, and blameless.
See the Lord’s patience as a chance for salvation, just as Paul, with the wisdom given to him, wrote to you.

f.g: Shows Paul’s letters were already circulating and respected.

chapters.n: Paul writes about these things in all his letters. Some parts are hard to understand, and ignorant, unstable people twist them as they do other scriptures—to their own ruin.
Since you have been warned in advance, be careful not to be carried away by the errors of lawless people and lose your firm footing.
Instead, keep growing in grace and in knowing our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ. To Him be glory now and forever.
